Issued at 211 AM CST Sun Nov 8 2026

This week into early next weekend (Saturday)...

Today: GOES East water vapor and RAP analysis indicate cold core 
upper low over the northeast and an upper low over the Sierra
Madres area of western Mexico. Colder air is situated across the
area this morning. Temperatures have fallen into the upper 30s to
low to mid 40s. High cirrus are situated across the area and will
continue to spreading across the region. 1024-1025mb surface high
will build in today, helping gradient winds to gradually relax
and lighten. Seasonable highs are expected today (upper 60s 
northwest of the Natchez Trace of Interstate 20 while upper 60s to
low 70s to the southeast). Seasonably cool lows are ongoing this
morning and again tonight (33F to 43F this morning and again
tonight). Patchy frost is possible this weekend as winds become 
calm tonight and effective radiational cooling remains likely. 
The dry soil conditions continue to support overachieving of the 
nocturnal cooling processes. At the same time, there remains 
potential for cirrus cloud decks to stubbornly stick around this 
weekend downstream of the SW US upper low, which could keep 
temperatures from dropping as much as they would in clear sky 
conditions. Putting these factors together yields uncertainty for 
low temperatures and potential frost impacts. Regardless, frost 
potential remains a concern, especially in low-lying and sheltered
areas. Kept inherited Limited HWO graphic for patchy frost during
these nights, mainly in north-central, east to northeast MS. 
Ensure plants are covered or indoors and take consideration of 
cold temperatures and impacts to pets and people with frost to 
light freeze potential.

This week into early next weekend: Quiet, cloudy and mostly dry 
pattern will persist this work week. Moist, isentropic ascent and 
cloudy conditions will remain draped across the Gulf Coast states 
through at least mid-week (Wednesday). Isolated rain shower is 
possible around midweek, but probs remain isolated and low (less 
than 15 percent). Upper low is still projected to become open 
shortwave, with less prominent ascent as it propagates eastward. 
With some thermal temps aloft warming, highs will moderate to 
seasonably through mid week (69F to 78F Monday to 73F to 80F by 
Wednesday). Lows will remain seasonable. The synoptic pattern will
feature a brief shortwave ridge passage early week before the 
eastern half of the country becomes dominated by deep layer 
troughing. With limited airmass recovery in the boundary layer 
likely under this suppressed regime, a drier and cooler pattern 
into late week continues to look likely. However, recent trends 
of stronger positive vorticity advection, moist ascent/convergence
along a cold front lend support of light rain shower development 
late week around Thursday. Global model guidance is beginning to 
pick up on this in the last run or so, but rain less than a tenth
of an inch north of Interstate 20. Unfortunately, this will make 
no dent in ongoing drought concerns. Another round of patchy frost
or light freeze remains possible in the day 6-8 range. Blended 
guidance probs of a light freeze are a medium to high chance (40 
to 70 percent) for central east and north-northeast MS, while 
falling at 30 degrees or below are low to medium chance (20 to 50 
percent). The growing season concerns will persist, so HWO 
graphics for frost/freeze are possible, with potential for 
heightened messaging. Will continue to monitor trends and hold off
for now this far out. Winds generally will be light through much 
of the period but clear days with full sun and associated deep 
mixing with little rain in sight could result in increased 
wildfire danger by Friday. /DC/86/
